record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: In the same setting of nowhere-zero divergence-free vector fields on a compact connected oriented manifold M^n with n ≥ 3 and Euler characteristic 0, does there exist such a vector field whose flow is volume-ergodic?

evidence.quote: Does there exist vector-fields as above such that the flow fXt is μ-ergodic ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a compact connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n \ge 3$ with Euler characteristic $\chi(M)=0$, equipped with a smooth volume form $\mu$. Consider smooth vector fields $X$ on $M$ that are (i) nowhere zero and (ii) divergence-free with respect to $\mu$ (so the flow $\{f_X^t\}$ preserves $\mu$). Does there exist such a vector field $X$ on $M$ whose volume-preserving flow $\{f_X^t\}$ is ergodic with respect to $\mu$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution. The question of existence, on every compact connected oriented manifold of dimension $\ge 3$ with vanishing Euler characteristic, of a nowhere-vanishing divergence-free vector field whose flow is ergodic is a known open problem in smooth ergodic theory; no source confirming a complete solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Poincaré–Hopf theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A nowhere-zero vector field exists on a compact manifold iff its Euler characteristic vanishes.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the topological precondition (χ=0) but does not address ergodicity.
